title: Error bounds for the truncated Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff and Zassenhaus formulas in unitary problems
authors: A. Arnal, F. Casas, J. L. Ruiz-Benito
abstract: The Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) formula plays a critical role in many branches of mathematics and physics. It expresses the logarithm of the product of exponentials of non-commuting operators as an infinite series of nested commutators of the operators involved. The Zassenhaus formula is the dual of the BCH formula: the exponential of a sum of operators is written as an infinite product of exponentials involving the operators and their commutators. In practical computations, however, one typically has to truncate the expansions, and so understanding the error committed by the resulting approximations and eventually providing suitable bounds for this error is of paramount interest. In this work we present a general strategy to derive rigorous error bounds and explicit error constants for the BCH and Zassenhaus formulas when the operators involved are skew-adjoint, as is the case for quantum evolution problems.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to calculate precise error bounds when approximating complex unitary time evolution operators using truncated versions of the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff and Zassenhaus formulas. By bounding the error in terms of nested commutators, it provides crucial theoretical guarantees for numerical quantum simulation techniques.
main_problem: The core problem is deriving rigorous, general error bounds for approximating the logarithm of operator products (BCH) or the exponential of sums (Zassenhaus) when these infinite series must be truncated for practical computation.
main_result: The authors provide a general strategy and explicit formulas showing that the truncation error can be bounded by linear combinations of nested commutators, which exhibit a predictable scaling property.
method: The analysis relies on comparing two representations of the evolution operator (e.g., $e^A e^B$ vs. $e^{\Phi(A, B)}$) and using differential equations satisfied by time-dependent unitary operators to bound the difference.
model_or_system: The context is general unitary problems in quantum physics where the evolution operator is expressed as a product or sum of exponentials of non-commuting, skew-adjoint operators (e.g., $e^{tA}e^{tB}$).
key_observables: The error norm, $\| 	ext{Exact Evolution} - 	ext{Truncated Approximation} \|$, which is shown to be related to the $(m+1)$-th order term in the expansion.
important_parameters: The truncation order ($m$ or $q$) and the norms of the involved operators ($\|A\|, \|B\|$).
main_assumptions: The operators $A$ and $B$ are assumed to be skew-adjoint, which is typical for quantum evolution problems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that the theoretically derived error bounds closely match the actual computed errors for small truncation orders ($m=2, 3$), confirming the accuracy of the established bounds.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the general theory by first establishing the framework using differential equations, then deriving specific, increasingly complex error bounds for both the BCH and Zassenhaus formulas in terms of nested commutators.
why_interesting: This work provides essential mathematical tools for quantum simulation algorithms (like Trotterization or product formulas) by quantifying exactly how much error is introduced when truncating the necessary exponential series expansions.
